findings: Unit economics are fine, fixed costs are not: quarter CM1 72.4%, CM2 57.0%, CM3 37.3% of net revenue (above typical Indian beauty D2C targets), yet EBITDA is -5.5% because salaries + opex eat ~43% of net revenue at ₹3.7 Cr/yr scale.

CM1/CM2/CM3 are not standardised in Indian D2C: sources disagree whether fulfilment sits in CM1 or CM2 and whether CM3 subtracts all marketing or only brand spend. We use CM1 = net - COGS, CM2 = - fees - shipping, CM3 = - all marketing, and test EBITDA = CM3 - salaries - opex.

'Orders' has three honest answers for October: 4,329 (P&L, excl. cancelled), 4,496 (all statuses) and 5,893 order lines. The eval question 'orders in October (all statuses)' scores against 5,893 lines, so a model that answers the P&L number fails it.
The README says stock cover is at the 'last-4-weeks rate' but divides by 29 days (Oct 3-31): Delhi SKU01 13.3 days at 29 days vs 13.1 at 28.

Platform-attributed ad revenue (₹46.7L) + creator coupon revenue (₹15.5L) cover only ~56% of net revenue (₹110.9L): blended ROAS 7.09x vs platform ROAS 2.98x. Attribution undercounts here, the opposite of the usual Meta over-claim story.
Creator ROAS on paid posts fell every month (2.95x Aug, 2.72x Sep, 1.88x Oct) while fees more than doubled (₹1.22L -> ₹2.76L); cost per coupon order rose from ₹400 to ₹549.
Over the quarter Flipkart, not the website, has the highest RTO (10.0% vs 9.6% of shipped orders); the website wins only in some months. Website COD RTO is 23.2% vs 1.3% prepaid (18x).
Cash is not the problem: ₹1.18 Cr cash / ₹2.03L average monthly EBITDA loss = ~58 months runway (38 above the ₹40L cash floor).
Speed: the 26-CSV parse costs ~110 ms of every kit call; caching to one SQLite file cut a cold kit sql from 199 to ~60 ms p50, of which ~50 ms is two Node process starts (the timeout watchdog child).
